title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Creamy fish and prawn pie with mash topping
excerpt: A proper British fish pie with chunks of salmon and cod in a parsley sauce, topped with fluffy mashed potato and baked until golden. Simple to prepare ahead and always satisfying.
sourceNotes: Fish pie is a traditional British dish with roots in the 19th century, when seafood was plentiful and inexpensive. The mashed potato topping became standard in domestic cookbooks of the early 20th century as a filling, economical way to stretch the filling.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie up to one day ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the bake time if going straight from the fridge.

content.text: Poach the fish in the milk before making the sauce. This both cooks the fish gently and infuses the milk with flavour for the sauce.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into chunks, for the topping

content.text: Preheat the oven to 200 C. Boil the potatoes until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain, return to the pan, and mash with 40 g of the butter, a splash of milk, and plenty of salt. Set aside.

Pour the milk into a wide pan and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the salmon and cod chunks, cover, and poach for 4 minutes. Lift the fish out with a slotted spoon, reserving the milk. When cool enough to handle, flake any larger pieces slightly.

Melt the remaining 40 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Soften the leeks for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the reserved poaching milk until smooth. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until thickened. Stir in the parsley and season well.
Fold the poached fish, raw prawns, and frozen peas into the sauce. Transfer to the roasting tin and spread the mash evenly over the top. Rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling around the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.fix: Add milk a little at a time and whisk well between each addition.

items.cause: Filling was too hot when mash was added
items.fix: Let the filling cool for 5 minutes before spreading the mash on top.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough or mash too thick
items.fix: Raise to 220 C for the last 5 minutes to brown the top.
